text.closed_only: Counts closed sessions only: Oct 20, 2026 close.
text.unit: 105 of 382 high-beta stocks climb on their own and beat both the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq 100
text.pic_note: The basket can still rise when only a few climb: the biggest winners carry it.
text.tldr: **27.5%** of high-beta stocks are climbing (105 of 382): **normal**. A month ago it was 25.9%. The basket closed 11.9% below its record close (Aug 17, 2026). Over the last 2 years it is lower than on 78% of days. But it is not rare over the long run: near the middle (higher than on 50% of days) since 2013, and 2022 spent 222 days below it. For S&P 500 stocks it is 12.4% (thin).
text.from: The TET Radar tab's trend check on the 388 high-beta stocks; dashed = S&P 500 stocks, the TET Radar tab's own reading.
text.how: Each of the 388 high-beta stocks gets the author's TET trend check. It counts as **climbing** only if it rises on its own chart **and** beats both the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq 100. The line is the share that does. High = most of them pull together; low = a few carry the group. When a few leaders sprint ahead, almost nobody can keep up, so the line sinks even while the basket climbs.
text.cases_note: Look-alike = the first close this low after a long stretch above it, with the basket near its 1-year high. Dip = the basket's lowest close in the next 3 months.
text.data: Data: today's 388 high-beta stocks (today's lists back in time), on the TET Radar tab's stock setup (own trend, vs the S&P 500, vs the Nasdaq 100), 2013 to Oct 20, 2026. A stock counts once it has enough history for the check and only on days it has a bar. Stock prices: daily closes; S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100: daily index closes. Dashed line = the TET Radar tab's own S&P 500 reading.

rules.above: A stock is above its 20-, 50-, 100- or 200-day average when its close is above the simple average of that many closes. A stock with a shorter history counts as above, in the total.
rules.members: Today's AI-basket, semis and high-beta lists carried back in time; each stock counts from its first clean bar (after a pre-listing stub, a SPAC shell or a long gap in its bars).
rules.series: Each group's line starts on the first day of 2013 with enough stocks to count.
rules.washout: Washout = the 50-day line drops to a deeply washed-out level after it had recovered since the previous washout. Ring = the deepest close of a washout that had not reset, when it came clearly later and lower.
rules.zones: Zones of the 50-day line, from low to high: washed out · weak · mixed · broad · very broad.
rules.percentiles: Percentile = the share of closed days (candles) since the series start / since 2021 at or below the reading; low = rare. An open candle is ranked against the closed ones.
rules.candles: Weekly / 2-week / monthly breadth = the daily reading on the candle's last day.
rules.kdjwash: KDJ washout meter = the share of the group's stocks that are maxed-out oversold on the KDJ of that candle size; a stock counts once it has enough candles. The weekly meter has ARMED and STRONG lines; the daily, 2-week and monthly lines are set to be as rare as the weekly ones.
rules.newlows: New 52-week low = the day's low at or below the stock's lowest low of the past year (a young stock: since it started trading). Bigger candles count each stock once when it made a new low inside the candle.
rules.after: After past washouts: the price about 1, 3 and 6 months later, the worst close within 6 months (none = never below the washout day's close), and how many sessions the 50-day line took to recover.
rules.thin: Thin rally check: the price near its 52-week high while few of the group's stocks are above their 200-day average; a big drop = a fall from that day's close within the next 3 months.
rules.thrust: Thrust: the 50-day line jumps from washed-out to strong within a few weeks; a new thrust needs a few months since the last one.
